skill.name: list-hygiene-monitor
skill.description: Monitors email-list decay, bounce and complaint trends, suppression drift, and engagement cohorts to produce re-permission, sunset, and pruning worklists.
skill.summary: Track recurring email list health and create evidence-based hygiene actions.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting and fixed repository-relative links. Two findings are confirmed: line 52 uses an unquoted user-derived command argument, and line 70 creates a save path from an unsanitized value. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The connector command accepts an unquoted list placeholder that may contain shell metacharacters.
remediation.suggestion: Validate list names, pass them as quoted arguments, and avoid shell interpolation when invoking connector or ledger scripts.

remediation.issue: The save filename includes an unsanitized list or topic value.
remediation.suggestion: Slugify the value, reject separators and dot segments, resolve the path, and verify it remains under the intended memory directory.

content.user_title: Monitor Email List Health and Decay
content.value_statement: Aging subscribers, rising bounces, and suppression drift can damage email delivery. This skill turns ESP exports and prior baselines into measured cohorts and action worklists.
actual_capabilities: Groups subscribers into active, cooling, dormant, deep-dormant, and never-engaged cohorts.
Compares hard-bounce and spam-complaint rates with benchmarks and prior baselines.
Checks suppression-list growth and identifies possible opt-out leakage.
Creates sized re-permission, sunset, and prune worklists.
Labels cohort counts and derived rates as measured or estimated.
Produces SEND S list-hygiene and SEND E engagement-decay readings.
limitations: Requires an ESP engagement export or cohort counts for meaningful analysis.
Cannot calculate trend changes without a prior baseline.
Does not run email authentication checks or compute a complete email quality score.
Does not modify the consent registry or execute reactivation campaigns.

use_cases.title: Track Newsletter Decay
use_cases.description: Review monthly engagement cohorts and identify subscribers moving toward dormancy.

use_cases.title: Protect Campaign Deliverability
use_cases.description: Compare bounce and complaint trends before planning the next promotional campaign.

use_cases.title: Audit Suppression Drift
use_cases.description: Reconcile active recipients with opt-out history and prepare a remediation worklist.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Export
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ESP engagement export for [list]. Group subscribers into 30, 90, 180, and 365-day cohorts. Label measured and estimated values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current list health

prompt_templates.title: Compare a Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [current report] with [prior baseline] for [list]. Calculate bounce, complaint, and cohort changes. Mark missing evidence as NEEDS_INPUT.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Action Worklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [engagement export], [bounce report], and [suppression history]. Create sized re-permission, sunset, and prune groups. Explain each rule using measured evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scheduled Watch
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a [monthly or quarterly] hygiene watch for [program and goal]. Define baselines, thresholds, suppression checks, SEND readings, handoffs, and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: A newsletter list has 20,000 subscribers with last-open and last-click dates.
output: Active: 11,500 measured; cooling: 3,500 measured; dormant: 2,700 measured.

output_examples.input: Current complaints are 0.12 percent, but no prior report is available.
output_examples.output: Complaint status: partial or watch. Trend status: NEEDS_INPUT because no prior baseline was supplied.

output_examples.input: The suppression record contains 48 addresses that remain on the active send list.
output_examples.output: Suppression leakage found for 48 addresses. Hold the next send, remove affected recipients, and route the evidence to the email quality auditor.

best_practices: Provide current exports and a dated prior baseline.
Separate measured values from estimated rates.
Review suppression leakage before starting re-permission activity.
anti_patterns: Do not invent trend deltas when baseline data is missing.
Do not re-permission addresses that bounced or complained.
Do not treat a point-in-time hygiene report as a complete deliverability audit.

faq.question: What data does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide engagement recency, bounce and complaint metrics, suppression history, and a prior baseline when available.

faq.question: Can it work without subscriber-level data?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use cohort rates, but it will label resulting counts or rates as estimated.

faq.question: Does it delete subscribers?
faq.answer: No. It creates worklists and recommendations. The user or email platform must apply changes.

faq.question: Does it check SPF, DKIM, or DMARC?
faq.answer: No. Use a deliverability pre-flight skill for authentication and infrastructure checks.

faq.question: How often should the monitor run?
faq.answer: High-frequency programs may need monthly checks. Newsletters often use quarterly checks, while outbound programs can review after each sequence.

faq.question: What happens when no baseline exists?
faq.answer: The skill reports current values and marks trend analysis as NEEDS_INPUT. The current run can become the next baseline.
